name: What rooms should I prioritize first in a whole-home renovation?

mainEntity.name: If I cannot renovate everything at once, which rooms should be prioritized first in a whole-home renovation?
mainEntity.text: If I cannot renovate everything at once, which rooms should be prioritized first in a whole-home renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prioritization should follow function and dependency. Kitchens and bathrooms usually come first because they are the most expensive to change later and often drive the rest of the layout. Core systems should also be handled early because plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and structural fixes must happen before drywall and finishes. If the project includes wall removal or additions, those decisions should be finalized before cosmetic selections. Once the functional backbone is set, you can move to flooring, cabinetry, tile, paint, and fixtures. A smart priority list helps avoid rework and keeps the budget focused on upgrades that improve daily use and long-term value.
acceptedAnswer.description: The kitchen, bathrooms, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC are usually the highest-priority parts of a whole-home renovation because they affect function, safety, and daily livability. After that, focus on flooring, storage, lighting, and any structural changes that must happen before finishes.
